title: Baseline the checks before the producer; mark failures pre-existing
summary: Athena will run the capability's checks on the base commit before the producer starts and record which fail. At verification, a check that failed on the base and still fails is marked pre-existing and no longer blocks the job. The verifier is then run and judges every acceptance criterion even when an unrelated check fails. Audience: Athena's maintainer, and verifiers reading the check results.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria require new tests plus cargo test, clippy and fmt passing.
Criteria check pre-existing marking and per-criterion judging by running tests, not by the existence of fields.
Fixes the `all_passed` gate that withholds judgment, not one failing check.
Behavior criteria name cargo commands the verifier can run.
One focused change in the run and check path, with no new config.
The rule is enforced in code and tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The baseline runs the same routed checks (crates/athena-core/src/routing.rs) in a snapshot of the base commit, before the first producer invocation in run.rs; a nested run skips it, as it already skips checks.
A check is pre-existing only if it failed on the base and fails again on the candidate, matched by name. A check that passed on the base and fails on the candidate is a real failure and still blocks.

Today verification runs the verifier only when every check passed (`if all_passed` in run.rs). That gate changes. When only non-pre-existing failures remain, the job still ends rejected, but the verifier runs and gives a verdict on each criterion. The verdict reaches the findings.
The baseline result is stored with the job's records, so it survives a restart and appears in the verifier brief as a labelled note on each check.
The user wants no new config key unless one is needed; the baseline always runs.
A baseline run that cannot start is recorded as 'baseline unavailable'. No check is then treated as pre-existing.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test using the fake agent and a check that fails on the base shows the base failure recorded before the producer's first invocation. Run `cargo test` and read the test.
A test shows a check failing on both base and candidate is marked pre-existing, in the verifier brief and in the check record. The job is not rejected for that check alone. Run `cargo test`.
A test shows a check that passes on the base and fails on the candidate is not marked pre-existing and still blocks the job. Run `cargo test`.

A test shows the verifier runs and returns a verdict for every acceptance criterion when an unrelated non-pre-existing check fails. The failing check is still reported and the job is rejected. Run `cargo test`.
A job whose base has no failing checks behaves as before: all checks run, and nothing is marked pre-existing. Run `cargo test`.
The check record or verification record carries a pre-existing marker and a note saying the check also failed on the base commit. The records are documented in docs/ and CHANGELOG.md.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass. Each new or changed module has tests.

out_of_scope: Fixing the checks that already fail on the base.
Changing which checks a capability defines, or the skip_when_only rules.
Changing the verifier's budget or the model's grants.
Re-running the baseline after a send-back or retry.
departures: Cost and time are higher than the reference. The change touches the core run loop, records and verifier brief, and needs new lifecycle tests. A cold build is also included. The verifier-gating change makes passing less certain.
